propositions.text: Appellant, a Pakistani citizen, appeals RPD decision denying refugee protection claim.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX (Appellant), a citizen of Pakistan appeals a decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) denying his claim for refugee protection.

propositions.text: Appellant has not submitted new evidence in support of appeal.
propositions.quote: He has not submitted new evidence in support of his appeal.

propositions.text: Appellant asks RAD to set aside RPD decision and substitute its own determination that he is a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: The Appellant asks that the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) set aside the decision of the RPD and substitute its own determination that he is a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant, a Pakistani citizen, appeals RPD denial of refugee claim without new evidence, asking RAD to substitute its own determination (court and applicant).

propositions.text: Appeal is allowed; matter referred to RPD for re-determination by different panel under IRPA s.111(c).
propositions.quote: This appeal is allowed. Pursuant to Section 111(c) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA), the RAD refers the matter to the Refugee Protection Division for re-determination by a differently-constituted panel.

paragraphs.summary: Appeal allowed; matter referred to RPD for re-determination by different panel under IRPA s.111(c) (court).

propositions.text: Appellant alleged he is Shia Muslim, worked for Sunni stepfather, and was attacked by Sunni extremists at Shia procession in 2010.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleged before the RPD that he is a Shia Muslim. He worked for his stepfather in Pakistan, who is a Sunni Muslim. He stated that on XXXX XXXX, 2010 he was at a Shia procession when Sunni extremists staged three suicide attacks in the middle of the congregation.

propositions.text: In 2012, extremists tried to stop peaceful gathering; appellant was beaten and police advised him to stay away from religious activities.
propositions.quote: He alleged that on XXXX XXXX, 2012, while in Gujarat, he was at the XXXX XXXX when extremists tried to stop the peaceful gathering outside. He tried to defuse the situation and was beaten. He was saved by the XXXX XXXX security. He filed a complaint at the police station and was advised to stay away from his religious activities.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant alleged Shia Muslim attacked by Sunni extremists in 2010 and 2012, police advised him to avoid religious activities (applicant).

propositions.text: Appellant organized Shia gatherings, was vocal, and was beaten in 2013 during a procession attacked by extremists.
propositions.quote: He began to arrange gatherings among Shia scholars, professors and prominent figures from his community. He was quite vocal at these gatherings. On XXXX XXXX, 2013 he was in XXXX for a week on business. He was a part of a procession when extremists began throwing rocks and shooting from the rooftop of the mosque. The claimant was identified and beaten by them.

propositions.text: In 2014, appellant hosted meeting to form NGO; Sunni extremists threatened his family to stop religious activities or face death.
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXX, 2014 he hosted a meeting at his house of prominent Shia community figures. The agenda of the meeting was to form a NGO. A couple of days later, people from the Sunni extremist group, Lashkare-e-jhangvi, came to his home and threatened his wife and children telling them that the claimant should stop his religious activities or he would face the consequences and be killed.

propositions.text: Police advised appellant to leave home and hide due to danger from powerful extremists.
propositions.quote: He reported the incident to the XXXX XXXX, who advised him to go to the police station to file a complaint and get police protection. The police advised him that these people were too dangerous and politically powerful and that they could track anybody. They advised him that it was best to leave his house and hide from them as this was happening to people all over the country.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant organized Shia gatherings, was beaten in 2013, threatened in 2014 by extremists; police advised hiding and leaving home (applicant).

propositions.text: Appellant received threatening call and gunshots fired at home; police advised him to leave home and country.
propositions.quote: The following night he received a threatening telephone call from the extremists. The same night gunshots were fired in front of the main gate of his home and a bullet shattered the rear glass of his car. He went to the XXXX XXXX the next day and told them about the threat and was advised that another member of that XXXX XXXX had been killed after receiving similar kinds of threats a little while ago. They advised him to leave his home immediately and if possible leave the country as well.

propositions.text: Appellant's stepfather helped him get Canadian visa; he left Pakistan to save his life.
propositions.quote: The claimant's stepfather helped him to get a Canadian visa and he left Pakistan to save his life.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant received threats and gunfire at home; police advised fleeing; stepfather helped get Canadian visa; appellant left Pakistan (applicant).

propositions.text: RPD heard appellant's refugee claim on January 13, 2015 and rejected it on February 26, 2015 for lack of credibility.
propositions.quote: The Appellant's application for refugee protection was heard on January 13, 2015. In a decision of February 26, 2015, the RPD rejected the claim finding the Appellant was not credible.

paragraphs.summary: RPD heard appellant's claim in January 2015 and rejected it in February 2015 for lack of credibility (earlier decision-maker).

propositions.text: RPD found appellant not credible due to delay in leaving Pakistan and claiming in Canada.
propositions.quote: The RPD found: a) The Appellant was not credible and lacked subjective fear in respect of his delay in departing Pakistan and the delay in making a claim upon arrival in Canada.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant's NGO luncheon activities not credible.
propositions.quote: b) The Appellant's activities in organizing a luncheon to establish an NGO were not credible.

propositions.text: RPD found threats from Sipah-E-Sahaba (SSP) not credible.
propositions.quote: c) The threats from Sipah-E-Sahaba (SSP) were not credible

propositions.text: RPD found appellant had viable internal flight alternative (IFA).
propositions.quote: d) The Appellant had a viable internal flight alternative (IFA)

paragraphs.summary: RPD found appellant not credible on delays, NGO activities, threats, and found viable internal flight alternative (earlier decision-maker).

propositions.text: Appellant submits RPD made unsustainable credibility findings on delays, hiding, membership, and threats.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits: 1. The RPD made unsustainable credibility findings in reference to the: * Delay in claiming protection in Canada * Delay in leaving Pakistan * Appellant's time in hiding * Appellant's membership in the XXXX XXXX * threats by the Lashkar-e-Jhangvi and the SSP.

propositions.text: Appellant submits RPD erred by failing to consider critical documentary evidence corroborating core allegations and contradicting credibility findings.
propositions.quote: 2. The RPD erred by failing to address or consider critical documentary evidence that corroborates the Appellant's core allegations and contradicts the RPD's credibility findings.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant submits RPD made unsustainable credibility findings and failed to consider critical documentary evidence (applicant).

propositions.text: Counsel made submissions on RAD's role reviewing RPD decisions.
propositions.quote: Counsel has made submissions in regard to the role that the RAD plays in the review of a RPD decision.

propositions.text: Huruglica decision guides RAD to conduct hybrid appeal reviewing all aspects and substituting its own decision if differing from RPD.
propositions.quote: Justice Phelan states in paragraphs 54 and 55 of the foregoing decision: [54] Having concluded that the RAD erred in reviewing the RPD's decision on the standard of reasonableness, I have further concluded that for the reasons above, the RAD is required to conduct a hybrid appeal. It must review all aspects of the RPD's decision and come to an independent assessment of whether the claimant is a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection. Where its assessment departs from that of the RPD, the RAD must substitute its own decision. [55] In conducting its assessment, it can recognize and respect the conclusion of the RPD on such issues as credibility and/or where the RPD enjoys a particular advantage in reaching such a conclusion but it is not restricted, as an appellate court is, to intervening on facts only where there is an "overriding and palpable error".

paragraphs.summary: Counsel submitted on RAD's role; Huruglica guides RAD to conduct hybrid appeal and substitute decision if differing from RPD (court and prior authority).

propositions.text: Federal Court allows RAD to apply either standard of review pending final judgment on scope of appellate review.
propositions.quote: Justice Martineau in Alyafi2 has said that, in the face of this conflict, the Federal Court should allow the RAD to apply either approach as long as the question of the scope of the appellate review of the RPD's decisions has not been settled by a final judgment by the Federal Court of Appeal or the Supreme Court of Canada.

paragraphs.summary: Federal Court allows RAD to apply either standard of review pending final judgment on appellate review scope (prior authority).

propositions.text: RAD will conduct own assessment and afford deference to RPD credibility findings or where RPD has advantage.
propositions.quote: Accordingly, the RAD will conduct its own assessment of the RPD's decision and come to an independent assessment of whether the Appellant is a Convention refugee or a person is need of protection. Deference will be afforded to the credibility findings of the RPD or to other findings where the RPD has a particular advantage in reaching its conclusions.

paragraphs.summary: RAD will independently assess RPD decision, affording deference to RPD credibility findings or where RPD has advantage (court).

propositions.text: RPD found credibility and internal flight alternative in Islamabad were determinative issues.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the determinative issue in this claim was credibility and the availability of an IFA in Islamabad.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found credibility and internal flight alternative determinative issues (earlier decision-maker).

propositions.text: Appellant submits RPD erred by failing to consider critical documentary evidence corroborating core allegations and contradicting credibility findings, constituting reviewable error.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits the RPD erred by failing to address or consider critical documentary evidence that corroborates the Appellant's core allegations and contradicts the RPD's credibility findings. The Appellant argues that this constitutes a reviewable error.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant submits RPD erred by failing to consider critical documentary evidence contradicting credibility findings (applicant).

propositions.text: RAD finds appellant's argument that RPD erred in failing to consider corroborating evidence has merit.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds the Appellant's argument has merit.

paragraphs.summary: RAD finds appellant's argument that RPD erred in failing to consider corroborating evidence has merit (court).

propositions.text: Appellant identified seven documents corroborating core allegations including letters, medical reports, police report, and court order.
propositions.quote: The Appellant identified seven documents that corroborate the Appellant's core allegations: * A letter from the editor of the magazine where the Appellant worked, confirming that he was targeted and denied protection by the police.3 * A letter from the Appellant's Iman, confirming events involving extremists on XXXX XXXX, 2012.4 * A medical report corroborating the Appellant's injuries on XXXX XXXX, 2012.5 * A letter from the XXXX confirming they urged the Appellant to flee Pakistan.6 * A medical report corroborating injuries in an incident in XXXX 2012.7 * A police report concerning the events of XXXX XXXX, 20148 * A court order ordering the XXXX police to provide protection to the Appellant and his wife. 9

paragraphs.summary: Appellant identified seven documents corroborating core allegations including letters, medical reports, police report, and court order (applicant).

propositions.text: Appellant submits RPD expressed reliability concerns about court order and did not address AIF findings or related findings in Reasons.
propositions.quote: In particular the Appellant submits that the RPD during the hearing expressed reliability concerns with the court order10 submitted by the Appellant concerning his step-father approaching the court in XXXX, Pakistan and seeking police protection for the threats against the Appellant. The Appellant notes that the RPD considered this document so important to the claim that it was decided the court order would be sent to Pakistan for verification. The Appellant argues that the RPD did not address the AIF findings in its Reasons, nor did it address any findings associated with this document.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant submits RPD expressed concerns about court order and failed to address AIF findings or related findings in Reasons (applicant).

propositions.text: RPD held mid-hearing conference, initiated AIF request to verify court documents, explained process, and adjourned hearing awaiting AIF results.
propositions.quote: The RAD has reviewed the audio recording of the hearing, which confirms the RPD held a mid-hearing conference with the Appellant's counsel and identified that there were concerns with the documents. The RPD on the record explained that it was going to initiate an Access to Information Form request (AIF) to ascertain the provenance of the court documents. The RPD subsequently explained the process to the Appellant, prepared the required forms and obtained the Appellant's signature to initiate the inquiry. The RPD continued the hearing and sought submissions from Appellant's counsel aside from the documents sent for the AIF. The RPD explained on the record that it anticipated receiving the AIF in approximately one month. The RPD further noted upon receipt of the AIF results it would contact Appellant's counsel and seek submissions on the finding. The RPD then noted that it would then decide on whether additional action was needed. The RPD also explained that if the AIF results were not received in a timely manner that it would assess what further action was to be taken. The hearing was then adjourned waiting for receipt of the AIF documents.

paragraphs.summary: RPD held mid-hearing conference, initiated AIF request to verify court documents, explained process, and adjourned hearing awaiting AIF results (court).

propositions.text: RPD failed to communicate AIF results or seek submissions before deciding; violated natural justice principles.
propositions.quote: The RAD examined the record and finds no additional information was communicated to the Appellant or his counsel. The RAD finds the RPD had a duty to communicate information to the Appellant and his counsel and seek submissions in respect to the AIF request or any decision made in respect of choosing to render a decision in the absence of the AIF. The RAD finds the RPD has violated the principles of natural justice by making its determination without considering the submissions of Appellant's counsel or at the very least explaining why it chose to dispense with the AIF request and how it assessed the document in rendering its decision.

paragraphs.summary: RPD failed to communicate AIF results or seek submissions before deciding, violating natural justice (court).

propositions.text: RPD selectively used supporting documents and did not address credibility or probative value of appellant's additional documents.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes in its review of the audio recording of the hearing that the RPD did address a number of the documents listed above by the Appellant in its questioning. The RAD having reviewed the RPD Reasons finds the RPD has arrived at credibility conclusions in its decision through selectively utilizing supporting documents. The RAD further finds that the RPD did not address whether it found the Appellant's additional supporting documents credible and/or probative in reference to the basis of his claim for refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: RPD selectively used supporting documents and did not address credibility or probative value of appellant's additional documents (court).

propositions.text: Karim v Canada requires tribunal to consider evidence corroborating testimony that contradicts its findings; ignoring such evidence is error.
propositions.quote: The RAD has considered the statements of the Federal Court in Karim v Canada:11 More importantly, however, I find that the Board erred in failing to refer to evidence that corroborated the Applicant's testimony but contradicted the Board's findings. It is not necessary for the Board to refer to every document in the decision, since there is a presumption that the Board has considered all the evidence: see Hassan v Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration) (1992), 147 NR 317, at para 3 (FCA); Lewis v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2004 FC 1195, at para 19. However, the more important or relevant the evidence is to a central issue, the more likely a Court will infer from the Board's silence that the evidence was ignored: Cepeda-Gutierrez v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) (1998), 157 FTR 35, at paras 15-17 (FCTD). In particular, where the Board fails to refer to evidence that contradicts its conclusion, it may be easier to infer that the Board overlooked this evidence. Moreover, it is an error to say there is "no evidence" of an allegation when there is in fact some evidence: Abdi v Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration) (1993), 68 FTR 319 (FCTD).

paragraphs.summary: Karim v Canada requires tribunal to consider evidence corroborating testimony that contradicts its findings; ignoring such evidence is error (prior authority).

propositions.text: RPD needed to explain why it did not assess key documents before making credibility findings fatal to the claim
propositions.quote: it was necessary for the RPD to provide a rationale for why it chose not to assess documents, which address issues that are central to the claim, prior to making determinative credibility findings that are fatal to the claim

propositions.text: RPD used credibility findings to support internal flight alternative findings
propositions.quote: The RPD subsequently utilized aspects of the credibility findings to ground its internal flight alternative findings

propositions.text: RPD failed to address appellant's personal documentary evidence and preference for some evidence over others
propositions.quote: In failing to address the Appellant's applicable personal documentary evidence in its reasons, and how this evidence undermines or, why it preferred some documentary evidence over other evidence, the RPD has failed to demonstrate that it has fairly assessed the evidence in the record

propositions.text: RPD's unsustainable credibility findings make the internal flight alternative finding unsustainable
propositions.quote: the RPD's application of the unsustainable credibility findings to the Internal Flight Alternative (IFA) finding, renders the IFA finding unsustainable

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD failed to explain ignoring key documents, misused credibility findings, and made unsustainable internal flight alternative findings.

propositions.text: RPD's credibility findings cannot be sustained
propositions.quote: the RPD's credibility findings in this regard cannot be sustained

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD's credibility findings unsustainable.

propositions.text: RPD decision must be set aside
propositions.quote: the RAD finds the RPD decision must be set aside

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the RPD decision must be set aside.

propositions.text: Section 111(1) IRPA allows RAD to confirm, set aside and substitute, or refer back RPD decisions
propositions.quote: Section 111(1) of IRPA allows the RAD to: (a) confirm the determination of the Refugee Protection Division; (b) set aside a decision of the RPD and substitute a determination that, in its opinion, should have been made; (c) refer the matter back to the RPD, giving the directions to the RPD that it considers appropriate

paragraphs.summary: The court states Section 111(1) IRPA permits RAD to confirm, set aside, substitute, or refer RPD decisions.

propositions.text: RAD can only refer back if RPD decision was wrong and RAD cannot confirm or substitute without hearing evidence
propositions.quote: The RAD can only make the referral described in 111(1)(c) if it was of the opinion that the decision of the RPD was wrong in law, in fact, or in mixed law and fact, and if the RAD cannot make a decision to confirm or substitute the RPD's decision without hearing evidence that was presented to the RPD

paragraphs.summary: The court explains RAD referral requires RPD decision to be wrong and inability to decide without evidence rehearing.

propositions.text: Appellant asks RAD to substitute its own determination that he is a Convention refugee
propositions.quote: The Appellant asks the RAD to substitute its own determination that he is a Convention refugee

propositions.text: RAD is not able to substitute its own determination due to outstanding issues needing rehearing
propositions.quote: The RAD is not in a position to do so. There remain significant outstanding issues, which the RAD is not able to address without rehearing the evidence

paragraphs.summary: The appellant asks for substitution as a refugee; the court refuses due to outstanding issues needing rehearing.

propositions.text: Concerns include impact of genuine court documents on state protection and appellant's obligation to approach higher authorities
propositions.quote: If the RPD finds the court documents to be genuine, does this impact a component of state protection? For example: Does it place an onus on the Appellant to approach higher authorities if they fail to provide protection?

propositions.text: IFA assessment did not sufficiently explore appellant's ability to relocate to proposed IFA location
propositions.quote: The IFA assessment did not sufficiently explore the Appellant's ability to relocate to the proposed IFA location

paragraphs.summary: The court notes concerns about state protection implications of documents and insufficient IFA relocation assessment.

propositions.text: RAD has not questioned appellant and cannot make its own credibility finding
propositions.quote: The RAD has not seen or questioned the Appellant and is therefore in no position to make its own credibility finding on his refugee claim

propositions.text: RAD cannot substitute its own determination or find appellant a Convention refugee or person in need of protection
propositions.quote: For these reasons, the RAD cannot substitute its own determination for that of the RPD, and it cannot find the Appellant to be a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RAD cannot make credibility findings or substitute determination without questioning appellant.

propositions.text: RAD refers matter back to RPD for re-determination by different panel and allows appeal
propositions.quote: Pursuant to Section 111(c) of IRPA, the RAD refers the matter to the Refugee Protection Division for re-determination by a differently constituted panel. This appeal is allowed

paragraphs.summary: The court refers the matter back to RPD for re-determination and allows the appeal.
